answer_as_filed: Southern Ohio Medical Center (SOMC) is located in Portsmouth, Ohio and is a private nonprofit with a contract with the government. SOMC has forty-six (46) registered child sites serving patients in Southern Ohio and North-Eastern Kentucky. SOMC has been listed as a 340B covered entity since April 1, 2005. SOMC uses its 340B savings to stretch scarce Federal resources to reduce the cost of drugs to vulnerable patients and expand access to care by establishing primary care & selected specialty care services in under-served areas with significant indigent populations. SOMC's Specialty Pharmacy runs a patient-centered Chronic Disease Management program for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, hypercholesterolemia, atrial fibrillation, and congestive heart failure (CHF). SOMC has a Discharge Pharmacy near the Emergency Department (ED) with extended hours. This allows patients to pick up prescriptions before leaving the hospital and improves medication adherence. SOMC's "Meds to Beds" program enables patients to receive prescription education and medications at their bedside upon discharge. Financial assistance is provided to patients that can't afford their medication. SOMC has 8 open door retail pharmacies and has plans to continue to expand its retail pharmacy footprint in an effort to reach even more vulnerable patients in remote areas. The organization also operates an infusion center, an anticoagulation clinic, and an anti-arrhythmia clinic.  These services would not be viable without the 340B Program.
